campaign_spec.objective: Prove the gptqueue testing program's lifecycle-fault, conformance, and resource-bound suites pass on the current Linux host through one bounded read-only vitest execution, with controller-owned evidence, without any live server, live Redis db0, network egress, or target-source writes.

acceptance: The conformance run against the spawned server completes with zero failing scenarios, or failing scenarios are individually declared as documented deviations in the consumer attestation with the official output digest.
requirements.statement: The official MCP conformance suite (@modelcontextprotocol/conformance) runs against the spawned gptqueue-http server and its session-lifecycle scenarios pass, with any deliberate deviation (self-healing stale-id re-initialization) explicitly excluded and documented.

acceptance: The controller-observed vitest run of the full default suite reports zero failing test files and zero failing tests, with the runtime file skipped (GPTQUEUE_RUNTIME_TESTS unset).
requirements.statement: The full default vitest suite (unit, store, integration; runtime gated off) passes with zero failures on the current host.

acceptance: The controller-observed vitest run of tests/integration/faults.integration.test.ts includes passing cases asserting: tools/call with the pre-restart session id returns 404 after a real kill+respawn; re-initialize succeeds with a fresh id; the app-level session and mailbox state survive in Redis db15.
A case proves a client that never re-initializes recovers nothing and the server never returns a bare 400 for a known-shaped stale-session call.
requirements.statement: The lifecycle fault-injection suite proves the recovery contract: a stateful client holding a cached session id across a real server SIGKILL+respawn observes the spec 404, re-initializes successfully, and its app-level registration and mailbox survive in Redis.

acceptance: tests/resource-bounds.test.ts passes: N initialize-without-DELETE cycles leave /health sessions at or below the cap; an abandoned session's server-side lease refresh stops after eviction (no gptq:lease refresh beyond TTL).
A Redis outage mid-request produces a bounded typed error to the client (never a hang, never silent data loss).
requirements.statement: The transports map is bounded (cap + LRU eviction), dead POST-only client sessions are reaped via refresh-on-request so Redis TTLs expire, and a Redis outage mid-flow produces a clean typed failure rather than a hang, all pinned by tests.
